policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'this house' does not distinguish the qere הזאת from the ketiv הזאתה; no mapped textual note decides the form, so both readings remain compatible and the base fallback is retained.
The ASV note explicitly says 'Hebrew Micaiah,' which distinguishes the ketiv מיכיה (Micaiah) from the qere מיכה (Micah) and selects r01.
